title: Chapa - engineering impact you and your agent shape together
pitch: Your repos show what you shipped. Chapa shows the engineer behind them: a live, verifiable impact badge that AI agents can understand, explain, compare, and evolve with you.
about_excerpt: Your repos show what you shipped. Chapa shows the engineer behind them: a live, verifiable impact badge that AI agents can understand, explain, compare, and evolve with you. Like 4 Comment 2 Story Updates Chapa meets WebMCP: the live developer-impact site becomes agent-operable. 19 tool registrations, reads open, writes human-approved. 18 distinct tools across 4 surfaces: discovery, profiles, verification, and the badge studio; all callable from the page itself. Agents propose, humans approve: simulate and preview freely, but nothing persists without explicit human confirmation. Try it live at chapa.thecreativetoken.com. Point any WebMCP-capable agent at the site or scan the QR. Inspiration Your repos show what you shipped. They do not show the engineer behind them. A CV can say "reliable," "consistent," or "quality-focused," but those are claims. Chapa tries to turn the work itself into evidence. Chapa analyzes 12 months of engineering activity and builds an Impact Profile across four core dimensions: Delivery, Quality, Consistency, and Breadth. An optional fifth dimension, Craft, appears when a developer provides a report from an AI coding tool. The profile includes a developer archetype, composite score, and trend over time. An internal confidence score adjusts the composite when data is incomplete. GitHub can be the starting point, but the profile is not limited to GitHub. Chapa can combine activity from GitLab, Bitbucket, Codeberg, and enterprise-managed GitHub accounts uploaded through the Chapa CLI. The result is a live SVG badge that can sit in a README and evolve as the developer's work evolves. Badges marked Verified metrics carry an HMAC-SHA256 signature, so their verification records can be authenticated and tampering detected. But there was a problem. The badge could show your engineering impact, but it could not explain it. Why is Quality 62? What caused the score to fall this month? What would happen if Delivery improved by ten points? How does this profile compare with another developer's? A static badge cannot answer those questions. An agent can. Why WebMCP WebMCP changes Chapa from something an agent can merely look at into something an agent can understand. Behind the badge is structured state: dimension scores, normalized submetrics, archetype, confidence, trend history, verification data, and badge configuration. Trying to infer that state from the DOM would be fragile and incomplete. With WebMCP, Chapa exposes the underlying model directly. An agent can call explain_dimension and receive the score, formula, normalized submetrics, and an improvement tip. It can call get_impact_history to reason about changes over time, or compare_profiles to compare two developers dimension by dimension. The agent is no longer interpreting pixels. It is working with the same engineering model that produced them. Creator Studio made the fit even stronger. Studio was already terminal-first: users type commands such as /set colorPalette indigo or /preset holographic . That command registry already defined Chapa's mutation vocabulary. WebMCP became another interface to the same system rather than a separate agent API. Human clicks, terminal commands, and agent tool calls all converge on the same underlying actions. What people and agents can do together Understand the profile Instead of searching through panels, you can ask: "Why did my score drop this month?" The agent can inspect the impact history, explain the affected dimensions, and answer using the same numbers Chapa displays. suggest_improvements runs Chapa's existing insight engine against the real profile, so recommendations come from the developer's own activity rather than generic advice. Explore what could change simulate_score lets an agent change hypothetical dimension values and calculate the resulting composite score, tier, and delta. Nothing is persisted. That means the agent can answer questions like: "What happens if I improve Quality to 80?" before anything changes. Compare engineering profiles compare_profiles validates another public handle, loads both profiles, and returns the delta for every dimension. What previously required opening two profiles and comparing them manually becomes a structured question an agent can answer. Understand verification explain_verification explains what a Chapa signature proves, what it does not prove, when the verification record expires, and whether it uses the current or legacy format. Verification becomes something a person can actually understand rather than just a cryptographic status indicator. Shape the badge Creator Studio contains seven visual style categories. Instead of navigating controls, a developer can describe what they want: "Make it minimal, remove the glow, and use the terminal preset." The agent translates that intent into the same /preset and /set commands a person would type. Those commands appear in the Studio transcript as they execute. The agent does not get a secret mutation path. It uses the same one the human does. Human control stays at the boundary The most important design decision was deciding what the agent should not control. Agents can inspect, explain, compare, simulate, preview, and restyle freely. Persistence is different. save_badge_config creates a proposal in the UI and waits for the developer to approve it. The agent can help shape the result; the human decides when it becomes real. In production, confirmation persists the configuration, invalidates the badge cache, and updates the public share page and live SVG. In judge demo mode, confirmed saves remain local. How I implemented WebMCP Chapa registers 19 WebMCP tool registrations across four surfaces, using 18 distinct tool names because Creator Studio and public profiles both register explain_dimension . Landing page ( / ) get_site_capabilities , find_profile Creator Studio ( /studio and /studio?demo=1 ) list_style_options , apply_badge_style , apply_preset , preview_badge , reset_badge_config , save_badge_config , simulate_score , suggest_improvements , explain_dimension Public profile ( /u/{handle} ) get_impact_profile , get_impact_history , verify_badge , compare_profiles , explain_dimension , get_embed_snippet Verification page ( /verify/{hash} ) get_verification_record , explain_verification A shared useModelContextTools hook registers each catalog on document.modelContext . A catalog signature keys registration so updated definitions register cleanly, and an AbortController removes tools when the component unmounts. In Creator Studio, Quick Controls, terminal commands, and WebMCP calls all resolve to command text and pass through the same executeCommand registry. This keeps the terminal transcript, React state, live preview, and pending save configuration on one shared mutation path. Trust and safety Public profile and verification tools are read-only. live_observation.first_impression: A developer-impact marketing page centered on generating and verifying GitHub-backed badges, with feature and agent-tool sections.
live_observation.after_state: The page remained on the landing content with no visible navigation or login transition in the observed state.
live_observation.notes: The purpose and available routes are clear, but the badge flow did not visibly advance.
